question: Which owner should recognize triggered editor text, retain its query, present current options and atomically accept completion across mounted views?
trigger: The user said go on the representation audit's proposed prototype of ordinary editor text with a view-local match.
requirements: Compose and edit native text without accepting completion during IME, including keyCode 229.
Every selectable result belongs to the current query; one owner controls input, filtering and open eligibility.
Completion uses a live target and one atomic inferred transaction, preserving rollback, stale-target refusal and one-step history.
Interaction, focus, query and popup belong to the exact mounted view and content root; remote ownership, read-only and authored projections remain correct.
Mention, slash, emoji and footnote retain their independent product catalog, ranking, insertion and focus laws.
Reconcile earlier work and keep historical execution, current source, behavior proof and adoption separate.
No product implementation, publication, search or AI product redesign in this assessment.
A transient draft must not leave a node in the shared document that no remaining collaborator can complete or cancel.
Results keep filtering while an IME composes the query, or the product explicitly accepts commit-time filtering.
evidenceReuse: Reused the representation audit's source census. Added a throwaway prototype on the real Plite editor (anchors, root views, history plugin) and one Chromium CDP composition check through the Plite browser handle. Read the existing combobox package spec, which captures the document right after the trigger and expects undo of a completion to return to it.
summary: Pursue ordinary editor text with a view-local match. A prototype that recomputes the match from the caret, stores only an Escape-dismissed trigger anchor and completes in one new-batch update passes ten headless checks on a real Plite editor: trigger rules, Escape suppression, remote-edit mapping and a dismissal that survives it, one-step completion undo that restores the typed query, callback rollback, stale-completion refusal and root-view switching that leaves literal text. The current native-input model instead restores an empty input on undo, losing the query. In Chromium with CDP composition, Plite keeps composing text out of the model until commit, so a model-read query pauses during IME composition; keep parity with a read of the mounted view's active composition text, which Plite's DOM input runtime already owns. The adoption plan replaces the four input schemas, author stamp, cancel API and native-input host lifetime, migrates stored input nodes to literal text, and still lands the model-independent defect fixes.

reconciliation.question: Which owner should recognize triggered editor text, retain its query, present current options and atomically accept completion across mounted views?
reconciliation.reason: The prototype settles the deferred representation question: ordinary text holds every tested law, and its one cost, model-read filtering pausing during IME composition, has a view-local owner in Plite.

reconciliation.question: Which owner should recognize triggered editor text, retain its query, present current options and atomically accept completion across mounted views?
reconciliation.reason: Supersede the design's native-input target and its private composition, gesture and interaction-lifetime machinery. Its defect diagnosis, Ariakit default-action cut and rejected global owners carry over.

reconciliation.question: Which owner should recognize triggered editor text, retain its query, present current options and atomically accept completion across mounted views?
reconciliation.reason: Retain the reproduced defects, atomic one-transaction completion with rollback and stale refusal, distinct feature policy and the rejection of a global manager, results service or InputRules takeover. Completion now targets the live match rather than an input node key.

alternatives: Keep the native input and build the design's Phase 1: loses on permanent complexity, the lost-query undo and orphaned author-locked input nodes; its one advantage is live filtering during composition.
Ordinary text reading only the model: holds every headless law but pauses filtering during IME composition; acceptable only as an explicit product call.
Ordinary text plus a mounted-view composition read in Plite (proposed): keeps live IME filtering with one substrate read; selected.
Add a global autocomplete manager, results service or InputRules takeover: rejected, as before.
proofLimits: Headless prototype on one paragraph leaf with real Plite anchors, views and history; queries split across marked leaves, multi-word queries and two DOM views of one root are untested. The composition result uses Chromium CDP synthetic IME, not a physical OS or mobile IME. The popup's Enter guard during composition, Ariakit integration, the composition read and stored-input migration are unbuilt. No product code changed.
